title: principles-core I/O seam registry (PRI-462)
description: Single source of truth for production files in packages/principles-core/src/ that are allowed to import fs/path. Both architecture-regression.test.ts and eslint.config.js derive their exemption lists from this file. To add a new I/O file, add it to the appropriate seam below — both guards update automatically.

seams.name: ledger-tree
seams.description: File-based principle ledger (principle_training_state.json). Single source of truth for parse, serialize, and mutate. Lives in core so pd-cli can read/write the ledger without importing openclaw-plugin private code. PRI-917 reuse retrieval joins this seam: it reads the same ledger document (read-only) so an existing-but-unparseable corpus fails closed instead of being reported as empty.

seams.name: sdk-store
seams.description: Standalone SDK store primitives exposed as package subpaths (evolution-store, trajectory-store, workflow-funnel-loader). Each reads SQLite or YAML directly so SDK consumers do not need the full openclaw-plugin runtime.

seams.name: sqlite-state-store
seams.description: Runtime V2 state.db connection factory and the RuntimeStateManager integration layer that wires all SQLite stores. Owns the DB lifecycle (open, pragma, close) for task/run/candidate/commit/artifact stores. PD v2 Phase 1: the intervention evidence ledger store joins this seam as a leaf store (all access through SqliteConnection; no direct fs/path).

seams.name: workspace-storage-paths
seams.description: Single source of truth for the workspace SQLite file locations (.pd/state.db and .state/trajectory.db). Imported by SqliteConnection, the SDK trajectory store, and every product read/write consumer in packages that depend on @principles/core, so relocating a database is one edit here instead of scattered path.join literals. No filesystem I/O: it only joins path segments.

seams.name: workspace-leak-guard
seams.description: Pure path-redirection helper that detects mock-leak workspace paths (e.g. '/fake/workspace', '/mock/state') used in test code and redirects them to a deterministic subdir under os.tmpdir(). Imports node:path for path joins and node:os for tmpdir(); performs no fs I/O itself. Called at every I/O entry point (SqliteConnection constructor, initTrajectorySchema, TrajectoryDatabase constructor, SystemLogger.log, EventLog constructor) to prevent Windows filesystem-root pollution.

seams.name: read-model
seams.description: Read-only composite models that query state.db and the file ledger to produce operator-facing snapshots (operator health, pain chain, pain recall, pruning, schema conformance, internalization chain integrity, activation compatibility). No writes — pure read paths exposed for CLI and console reuse. The pain-recall read model's temp-directory I/O is WAL read-only snapshot staging only (system temp root, cleaned on success and failure paths): the business workspace is never written, and a missing database is never created.

seams.name: diagnosis-evidence-read
seams.description: Read-only promoted governance-evidence window reader used by the diagnostician context assembler. It reads {workspace}/.state/trajectory.db governance_observations rows with retention_class='promoted' through the registered trajectory-store SDK seam (openTrajectoryDbReadonly). It owns no schema and never writes or creates the database: a missing file or table is reported as an observable degradation, never treated as an empty window.

seams.name: audit-observability
seams.description: Candidate/ledger consistency audit and pain-signal observability writers. These write trajectory.db pain events and events_*.jsonl for CLI and gate-block paths that lack the legacy SDK observability writers, closing the observability gap without importing openclaw-plugin.

seams.name: remediation-review
seams.description: Internalization integrity remediation (reads state.db, writes corrective task records) and append-only owner-action audit logs (governance recovery actions at .state/recovery_actions.jsonl). Both own file/DB writes that core runners, CLI commands, and console recovery endpoints trigger directly.

seams.name: test-infrastructure
seams.description: Shared Story A acceptance helpers under src/__tests__. They create temporary workspaces and SQLite stores for production-path tests, but are excluded from published runtime behavior.

seams.name: owner-identity
seams.description: Install-level Owner identity registration file (~/.pd/owner.json) per ADR-0022 (PRI-578). Lives in core so pd-console and pd-cli share the single resolver (env > file > none) with one tested implementation.

seams.name: pi-ai-http-transport
seams.description: LLM transport owner (PRI-683): builds the undici Agent-backed fetch injected into every pi-ai provider request via options.fetch, disabling Node global fetch's implicit 300s headersTimeout/bodyTimeout caps so runtimeProfile.timeoutMs is the single timeout authority. Registered seam because it imports the undici transport library (no fs/DB I/O; requests still go out through the pi-ai SDK).

namingPolicy.description: PRI-1104 naming policy consumed by scripts/check-naming-policy.mjs. PR-3 (PRI-1136) turned the runtime-v2 rule into a merge gate: the script runs --strict from verify:merge and fails on gated rules or scan I/O errors. Scan surface = packages/<pkg>/{src,scripts}/**, packages/<pkg>/tests/** (import rule only), root plugins/** (shipped payload), all package manifests beneath packages/ (including nested payload manifests), this registry, and .github/workflows/*.yml. Historical records (docs/, CHANGELOG, .gitleaksignore commit fingerprints) are out of scope on purpose. The identifier rule bans isRuntimeV2/RuntimeV2/runtimeV2/RUNTIME_V2 identifiers; only exact tokens listed in allowedIdentifiers are suppressed (the deprecated host-runtime export alias RUNTIME_V2_EVENT_LOG_CANDIDATE_DIRS and deprecated CLI JSON alias isRuntimeV2Exclusive). PRI-1139 (PR-6) turned versioned-output-ref into a merge gate: every production writer now uses the version-neutral canonical registry keys, so a versioned outputSchemaRef literal in source is a regression. The two plugin payload files in exemptFiles are a temporary exception: they must keep @principles/core/runtime-v2 until runtime-version.json pins move from core 4.1.0 to the Core 5.x release that ships the ./runtime subpath; the Core 5.x runtime-pins PR MUST remove those two entries. The full cross-package consumer list and the Frozen Wire Literals with their read/write sites live in docs/audit/PRI-1104-single-version-convergence-plan.md (§4, §8).
